A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NBDI research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation and robot-manipulation experiments, ablations, and analyses of decision points, dataset quality, and model capacity.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds SiMPL meta-reinforcement-learning experiments and a discrete-maze comparative case study.

M1.justification: Section 7 adds a SiMPL+NBDI integration, replacing SiMPL's fixed-length skill extraction with novelty-terminated skills for meta-learning. This is a limited pipeline adaptation; the standalone NBDI algorithms, novelty module, and losses remain unchanged. The expanded ELBO explanation already appeared in v1 Appendix B.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation from downstream policy learning to meta-training across maze goals and subsequent adaptation to an unseen target task. This adds substantially different task requirements. Existing navigation, manipulation, and MuJoCo coverage remains; discrete-grid analysis was already present in v1.

E2.justification: SiMPL becomes an evaluated comparator in Figure 9 and Table 2. Appendix G additionally evaluates a BPE-based compression proxy presented as illustrating LOVE's MDL principle, rather than LOVE's variational implementation. Comparator membership in the original benchmark comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 7 introduces a distinct evaluation design: meta-training on 10 sampled maze goals followed by target-task learning measured at specified episode counts. Appendix G adds comparisons using 100 versus 10,000 trajectories, relative-novelty windows of 2 and 7, and BPE merge counts of 20 and 100. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a focused case study examining termination locations and their sensitivity to trajectory count, transition-history windows, and compression settings. Existing threshold, termination-distribution, skill-length, suboptimal-data, and capacity analyses remain. Figure 8 redraws the retained capacity analysis rather than establishing a new robustness experiment.

E5.justification: The new SiMPL results report standard errors over three seeds, while existing learning comparisons retain five-seed 95% confidence intervals. Figure 8 replaces mean-and-standard-deviation error-bar plots with boxplots, without specifying their whisker convention. These are reporting changes, not evidence of increased runs for existing experiments.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial meta-learning results and discrete-maze termination maps. New Table 2 reports target-task success of 0.560±0.121 for SiMPL+NBDI versus 0.143±0.063 for SiMPL at episode 20, and 0.960±0.021 versus 0.593±0.191 at episode 100. These are newly reported comparisons; the original Figure 5 benchmark scores and Table 1 results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 5 narrows its explicitly stated data assumption from 'unstructured agent experiences' to 'task-agnostic, expert-level demonstrations.' The mathematical definitions, termination-improvement theorem, and learning-objective equations otherwise remain unchanged, with no new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions, and central conclusion retain the same claims about novelty-based termination, improved policy learning, and transfer across changed environment configurations. Changing 'efficient' to 'effective' and 'finding' to 'method' does not substantively redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F explicitly distinguishes adequate observation-space coverage from full downstream state-space coverage and explains differing demonstration requirements. Section 7 interprets the new results as supporting broader integration and knowledge transfer. Appendix G adds explanations involving transition-history dependence and compression, although its LOVE interpretation relies on a BPE proxy.

D1.justification: Appendix F newly discloses 85,000 maze, 37,000 stacking, and 400 kitchen trajectories. Appendix B.3 adds percentile guidance for the unchanged thresholds, and the reported code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository. However, the approximately 97th-percentile guidance conflicts with the retained top-1% statement in Appendix I.2.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Ajay et al. on offline skill execution and Gallé on BPE. SiMPL shifts from a future-work reference to an evaluated integration, while future work shifts toward offline skill execution. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, expands the main-text training description, and adds Section 7, Appendix B.3, Appendices F–G, acknowledgments, and an impact statement. Most existing prose and section organization remain intact; former Appendices F–G become H–I.

P2.justification: v3 adds the meta-training plot, target-task results table, and discrete-maze heatmaps. Figure 8 is redrawn with boxplots, explicit hidden-layer configurations, and a parameter-count axis; Figures 1–2 receive expanded captions. Most existing displays are retained, with renumbering and conference-format headers.

improvement.justification: v3 tests the meta-RL extension that v1 left as future work and improves reproducibility through dataset-size disclosures and additional guidance. These provide useful, limited gains while preserving the original evidence. The benefit is tempered by Appendix G's use of BPE to support conclusions about LOVE and the unresolved conflict between Appendix B.3's percentile guidance and Appendix I.2's top-1% statement.
